title: Forms and User Input
description: Learn how to create interactive HTML forms to collect user input efficiently and accessibly.

lessons.title: Introduction to HTML Forms
lessons.content: HTML forms allow users to enter and submit data to web servers. Forms are essential for user registration, login, feedback, and more.

lessons.title: Creating a Basic Form
lessons.content:
<form action="/submit" method="post">
  <input type="text" name="username">
  <input type="submit" value="Submit">
</form>
// The <form> tag defines a form with an action URL and method.

lessons.title: Text Inputs and Labels
lessons.content:
<label for="email">Email:</label>
<input type="email" id="email" name="email">
// Use <label> for accessibility and form usability.

lessons.title: Input Types in Forms
lessons.content: HTML supports many input types: text, password, email, number, date, file, checkbox, radio, and more, each tailored for specific data entry.

lessons.title: Checkboxes and Radio Buttons
lessons.content:
<input type="checkbox" name="subscribe" checked> Subscribe
<input type="radio" name="gender" value="male"> Male
<input type="radio" name="gender" value="female"> Female

lessons.title: Textareas and Multi-line Input
lessons.content:
<label for="message">Your Message:</label>
<textarea id="message" name="message" rows="4" cols="50"></textarea>

lessons.title: Form Attributes and Validation
lessons.content: Use attributes like `required`, `placeholder`, `min`, `max`, and `pattern` for client-side validation to improve data quality.

lessons.title: Grouping Inputs with Fieldset and Legend
Best Practices for Form Design
lessons.content: Ensure forms are accessible, mobile-friendly, clearly labeled, and include helpful validation messages and logical structure.
